title: Map a column’s terms to a vocabulary

configuration.note: The column is required; the column the links go into defaults to <column>_wikidata and is refused where the table already has one of that name. Every kept choice must be a Wikidata entity identifier. A choice may be null, which records that a person looked and judged that nothing in Wikidata names the term; that is held apart from a term nobody has looked up.

ports.note: One table in, the same table out with a link column added. The terms offered for linking are the distinct values of the chosen column, so the table must have run once before the dialog has anything to show.

ontology.note: Partial: every term the receipt asserts is declared in ontology/fieldwork.ttl, and no widget-specific SHACL shape checks the result. The activity asserts the column linked, the distinct, linked and unlinked term counts, the rows carrying a link, the authority, and what was chosen for each term with the date and how many candidates were on offer. Each chosen entity is also a subject carrying fw:namedByTerm, so a reader following the link sees what the term was taken to mean here.

changes.description: Each term in a column given the Wikidata entity a person judged it to name, so rows carry an identifier that means something outside this workflow (experiment 232). The choosing happens in Configure…; a run asks Wikidata nothing.

evidence.note: Unit tested offline: the distinct terms a person is asked about; a deliberate decision not to link held apart from a term nobody looked up; the link column added and refused where it would overwrite; the search parsed with properties and id-less rows rejected; and narrowing that reorders candidates without removing any. Measured 2026-11-24 against Wikidata's own search on four terms in hand: one top hit of four was wrong (Kano returns the city where an LGA table means the state, ranked fourth) and three of four carried a competing entity of another kind in the top four. NOT established: that Wikidata is right about anything, what share of terms resolve for any country, or that a generic client name satisfies Wikimedia's User-Agent policy for a tool many people may run. No worked example instantiates it yet.
